Home News Arts and Culture Business Sports Opinion Research Live TV/Radio Media Elections Dark Mode Dark mode --> Economy Output per worker stood at 178% in 2025 – GSS Source : Joy Business 20 November 2026 6:32pm ▶ Listen to this article Audio By Carbonatix
Output per worker in 2025 was 178% higher than in 1991, the Ghana Statistical Service has stated.
Over the same period, the Service said in its 2026 Productivity, Employment and Growth Report that the output rose by 38% in lower-middle-income Sub-Saharan African countries and by 31% in upper-middle-income ones.
Since 2013, output per worker has risen by 37%, from GH₵11,093 to GH₵15,197.
The report stated that productivity growth has relied heavily on capital .
“ Capital per worker rose almost fourfold between 1991 and 2025, from about GH₵9,000 to about GH₵35,000. The sources of growth have changed over time”.
It added that in the 2000s, growth came mainly from using resources more efficiently, whilst in the 2010s, it came mainly from adding capital.
Also, since 2020, capital per worker has grown by only 1.0% a year, and productivity growth has slowed with it.
The report continued that the economy now uses GH₵2.33 of capital to produce GH₵1 of output, compared with GH₵1.63 in 1991.
Again, productivity gains differ widely across sectors. Between 2013 and 2025, output per worker rose by 65.7% in agriculture, 47.3% in services and 28.7% in industry;
Information and communication had the fastest productivity growth, at over 20% a year, but it employs relatively few people.
The second edition of the Productivity, Employment and Growth Report answered both questions for Ghana over 35 years, from 1991 to 2025.
It combined the national accounts with four censuses and surveys, and followed methods set by the International Labour Organization and the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development.
